# Slashy Review 2026: Features, Pricing, and Verdict

t+t this+that team ·

Slashy Review 2026: Features, Pricing, and Verdict

Slashy is an AI email assistant. It drafts replies in your voice, triages what arrives, and handles the scheduling back-and-forth that eats a surprising share of the working day. It is a Y Combinator company and it is aimed squarely at people whose inbox is the job.

The category it sits in is crowded, so the useful questions are narrow: what does it actually do, what does a seat cost, what do people complain about, and where does it stop. Pricing was checked against Slashy’s own page on August 4, 2026.

## Key takeaways [...] One point in Slashy’s favor: they hold SOC 2 Type 2, where ours is Type I as of July 31, 2026 with Type II underway. Type II covers a period of operation rather than a single date, so if that is a gate for your buyer it is a difference and not one we can argue away.

## Who should choose Slashy?

Choose it if the bulk of your work arrives by email, replying is the bottleneck, and you want an assistant that produces sendable drafts without changing the client you use. The SOC 2 position makes it easier to get through a security review than several alternatives.

Look elsewhere if a real share of your work arrives in team chat, if the problem is commitments going missing rather than replies taking too long, or if $25 per seat is hard to justify across a team.
